observation_text: Child had trouble staying focused while getting dressed in the morning.
antecedent: Child was asked to get dressed for school.
behavior: Child was playing with toys instead of putting on clothes.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Gently reminded child to focus on getting dressed.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make morning routines more fun?
general_support_idea: Using a visual schedule for morning tasks can help.

observation_text: Child was hesitant to leave the house for school.
antecedent: Child was reminded it was time to leave for school.
behavior: Child refused to put on shoes and kept asking for more time.
consequence: No consequence noted
possible_trigger: Not wanting to leave favorite toys behind
caregiver_response: Encouraged child to pick a favorite pair of shoes.
suggested_followup_question: What activities can we do to ease transitions?
general_support_idea: Offering choices can improve the transition experience.

observation_text: Child was distracted by a new toy during breakfast.
antecedent: Child was sitting at the table for breakfast.
behavior: Child kept reaching for the toy instead of eating.
consequence: Child eventually finished breakfast after being reminded to eat.
possible_trigger: New toy was introduced the night before
caregiver_response: Prompted child to put the toy away until after breakfast.
suggested_followup_question: How can we minimize distractions during meals?
general_support_idea: Setting a designated playtime after meals might help.

observation_text: Child wanted to wear mismatched socks to school.
antecedent: Child was looking for socks to wear.
behavior: Child insisted on wearing socks that didn't match.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Acknowledged child's choice and let them wear the socks.
suggested_followup_question: How can we support their independence in dressing?
general_support_idea: Discussing personal style might encourage self-expression appropriately.

observation_text: Child took longer than expected to finish brushing teeth.
antecedent: Child was reminded it was time to brush teeth.
behavior: Child brushed teeth slowly while playing with the toothbrush.
consequence: Child eventually finished but we were late leaving for school.
caregiver_response: Set a timer for brushing teeth next time.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can help make hygiene routines quicker?
general_support_idea: Using a fun timer can enhance focus and efficiency.

observation_text: Child got upset when asked to clean up toys before breakfast.
antecedent: Child was playing with toys in the living room.
behavior: Child shouted and knocked over a stack of blocks in frustration.
consequence: Child calmed down after caregiver helped clean up.
caregiver_response: Helped child clean up and offered a choice of breakfast.
suggested_followup_question: What activities can help ease transitions?
general_support_idea: Offering a fun clean-up song can help.

observation_text: Child started running around the house instead of getting ready.
antecedent: Child was asked to start getting ready for school.
behavior: Child decided to chase the family dog instead of dressing.
consequence: Child finally got dressed after a few minutes of play.
caregiver_response: Redirected child to get ready with a game plan.
suggested_followup_question: What fun routines can we implement to keep them focused?
general_support_idea: Incorporating a game into routines could improve engagement.

observation_text: Child refused to put on a jacket when it was cold outside.
antecedent: Child was reminded to dress warmly.
behavior: Child insisted they were not cold and wanted to go outside without a jacket.
consequence: Child eventually agreed to wear a jacket after feeling the cold air.
caregiver_response: Compromised by letting child wear a light jacket.
suggested_followup_question: How can we prepare for unexpected weather changes?
general_support_idea: Discussing the weather the night before can help prepare them.

observation_text: Child attempted to climb a tree without supervision.
antecedent: Child was playing outside while caregiver prepared breakfast.
behavior: Child began to climb a tree that was too high.
consequence: Child was called down safely after being reminded of safety rules.
caregiver_response: Discussed safety and set clear boundaries about climbing.
suggested_followup_question: What conversations about safety can we have?
general_support_idea: Role-playing safety discussions can be helpful.

observation_text: Child was playing with their food at breakfast.
antecedent: Child was served pancakes for breakfast.
behavior: Child started making shapes with the food instead of eating.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Encouraged child to make a pancake face before eating.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make mealtime fun?
general_support_idea: Creating engaging meal presentations can improve eating behavior.

observation_text: Child was reluctant to leave the house without a special toy.
antecedent: Child was asked to get ready for school.
behavior: Child insisted on bringing a large toy that wouldn’t fit in their bag.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Suggested taking a smaller toy for comfort instead.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to ease the attachment to certain toys?
general_support_idea: Using a special bag for toys can help manage expectations.

observation_text: Child was overly excited and couldn’t sit still during breakfast.
antecedent: Child was given a favorite breakfast.
behavior: Child bounced in their chair and spoke non-stop about the day.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Gently reminded child to sit still while eating.
suggested_followup_question: How can we channel their excitement?
general_support_idea: Incorporating calm-down activities before meals could help.

observation_text: Child struggled to keep shoes on when leaving the house.
antecedent: Child was in a hurry to get to the store.
behavior: Child kept taking off shoes and trying to run ahead.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Encouraged child to keep shoes on and walk with me.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can help with keeping shoes on?
general_support_idea: Choosing shoes that fit well can help.

observation_text: Child tried to stay home instead of going to school.
antecedent: Child was reminded it was a school day.
behavior: Child cried and said they didn't want to go.
consequence: Child calmed down after discussing fun things to do at school.
caregiver_response: Offered a deal to do a fun activity after school.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help with morning motivation?
general_support_idea: Planning a reward for school days can provide motivation.

observation_text: Child locked themselves in their room during morning routine.
antecedent: Child was asked to start getting ready.
behavior: Child locked the door and refused to come out.
consequence: Child finally unlocked the door and came out after a few minutes.
caregiver_response: Discussed feelings about morning routines after.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to improve our morning communication?
general_support_idea: Creating a visual checklist can provide clarity.

observation_text: Child insisted on wearing pajamas outside.
antecedent: Child was getting ready to go outside.
behavior: Child argued about wearing outside clothes and wanted to stay in pajamas.
consequence: Child changed into appropriate clothes after a reminder.
caregiver_response: Gently encouraged the importance of dressing for the weather.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage proper dressing?
general_support_idea: Using fun clothing themes can help make choices easier.

observation_text: Child was distracted by a show while getting dressed.
antecedent: Child was given a time warning to dress for school.
behavior: Child kept asking for one more minute of the show instead of getting ready.
consequence: Child eventually turned off the show and got dressed.
caregiver_response: Set a timer for the end of the show next time.
suggested_followup_question: How can we keep them on track during morning routines?
general_support_idea: Incorporating favorite shows as rewards for finishing tasks can help.

observation_text: Child refused to eat breakfast because it was a new food.
antecedent: Child was offered a different kind of cereal.
behavior: Child pushed the bowl away and said they didn't want it.
consequence: Child eventually tried a spoonful after caregiver tasted it first.
caregiver_response: Modelled trying the food and encouraged them to taste.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do about trying new foods?
general_support_idea: Involving them in meal prep can increase willingness to try new foods.

observation_text: Child had difficulty finding their backpack on the way to school.
antecedent: Child was asked to get their things ready.
behavior: Child searched through several bags and got frustrated.
consequence: Child eventually found the backpack after looking with caregiver's help.
caregiver_response: Helped organize their things the night before.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we implement for better organization?
general_support_idea: Creating designated spots for school items can reduce chaos.

observation_text: Child became upset when told they needed to wear a hat.
antecedent: Child was reminded to dress warmly for the weather.
behavior: Child argued and threw the hat on the ground.
consequence: Child picked the hat back up and put it on after talking about the cold.
caregiver_response: Discussed the importance of staying warm.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage compliance with clothing choices?
general_support_idea: Using fun, colorful hats could entice them to wear them.

observation_text: Child was asked to get dressed but took a long time looking for clothes.
antecedent: Child was waking up and needed to change into clothes.
behavior: Child started playing with toys instead of getting dressed.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Caregiver gently reminded to keep looking for clothes.
suggested_followup_question: What clothes do you want to wear today?
general_support_idea: Set a timer for getting dressed to encourage quicker action.

observation_text: Child was playing outside and was told it was time to come in for breakfast.
antecedent: Child was having fun playing with friends.
behavior: Child refused to come inside and continued to play.
consequence: Child finally came in after caregiver had to go outside and call them several times.
caregiver_response: Caregiver went outside to help transition.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make coming inside easier next time?
general_support_idea: Establish a fun routine for coming inside.

observation_text: Child was waiting to brush teeth but got distracted by a toy.
antecedent: Child was asked to prepare for bed.
behavior: Child kept ignoring the request and continued to play with the toy.
consequence: Child finally put the toy down and walked to the bathroom after a few reminders.
caregiver_response: Caregiver provided a countdown to brushing teeth.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to make brushing teeth more fun?
general_support_idea: Create a visual schedule for bedtime activities.

observation_text: Child was playing outside and climbed onto a fence.
antecedent: Child was feeling adventurous during playtime.
behavior: Child climbed higher on the fence than allowed.
consequence: Caregiver quickly went over and helped the child down safely.
caregiver_response: Caregiver explained the dangers and helped them down.
suggested_followup_question: What are some safe ways to have fun outside?
general_support_idea: Teach the child about safe climbing practices.

observation_text: Child was at a store but ran off from the shopping cart.
antecedent: Child was bored during shopping.
behavior: Child left the shopping cart to explore the store by themselves.
consequence: Caregiver found the child in another aisle after calling their name.
caregiver_response: Caregiver discussed staying close in busy places.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make shopping more engaging for you?
general_support_idea: Plan engaging activities for store visits.
